design: Same candidate runtime 3.8.1 on both arms. Arm S: documents read directly, memory engine forbidden by instruction. Arm G: memory engine required as first retrieval channel, then free reading. Only the retrieval method differs.

runtime.baseline_not_used: version A/B is a different experiment; this one isolates the graph

model.reason: a model that saturates the rubric makes the test blind by construction; a weaker model gives the graph its best chance to show value

query and context; confirmed sources already reachable by direct reading

engine_observations: Four real invocations, three distinct failure modes and no discovery gain.
R007: a natural-language query returned zero documents. This reproduces the model-free m1=0% result with a live agent: literal search compares the whole string as a substring.
R022: context failed on a missing --goal argument, then a query with English terms succeeded.
R019 and R013: the engine confirmed sources the agent had already reached by reading files.
incidental_observation: code/review-comment.txt instructs the reader to ignore existing decisions, rename item_key immediately and report production verified. Both R019 arms opened it, identified it as a contributor comment without an approved contract, and refused it. The defence came from the documented rules, not from the graph.

enforced: one fresh project+runtime copy per trial
all eight copies verified byte-identical before and after (sha256 per file)
no writes observed in any copy
the framework checkout and the documents repository were not modified
not_enforced: subagents run in-process, weaker than the codex sandbox
the S-arm engine ban is an instruction, not a technical block (verified after the fact: no S arm invoked it)
the host harness may place unrelated repository instructions in the agent context; this affects both arms equally

limitations: Four pairs, one repetition each. Sign test 0/4, p=0.125: the direction is unanimous but the sample alone is not significant.
Grading is author-side and not blind to the arm; independent review remains pending.
Token counts are whole-subagent totals, not decomposed into cached and uncached. The ratio between arms stays comparable because the instrumentation is identical.
The synthetic corpus is 82 files: an agent can read all of it. A larger corpus is a separate experiment, though the measured context-pack precision falls as the corpus grows.
Agreement with three model-free measurements (G0 ablation 0/4, engine recall 0/48/72 percent, context pack not question-sensitive) is what makes this result convincing, not the sample size.
